hero.title: Himalayan Flood Disaster Deepens as Rescue Efforts Face Bad Weather
hero.description: A catastrophic glacier-related flood in the Himalayan region has killed more than 600 people and left nearly 3,000 missing across Nepal and Tibet. Bad weather is hampering rescue operations as Nepal seeks international technical assistance and estimates reconstruction could cost $4–5 billion.

featured.title: Himalayan Flood Disaster Deepens
featured.content: Nepal is facing a major humanitarian and reconstruction crisis after catastrophic flooding triggered by a glacier collapse. Bad weather has disrupted some search-and-rescue operations, while authorities seek international technical help.
featured.imageQuery: Nepal Tibet Himalayan flood disaster rescue

articles.title: BREAKING: Himalayan Flood Disaster Leaves Hundreds Dead and Thousands Missing
articles.description: A devastating flood triggered by a glacier collapse has killed at least 626 people in Nepal and seven in Tibet, while nearly 3,000 people remain missing. Bad weather is hampering rescue operations and Nepal is seeking international technical assistance.

articles.title: Nepal Estimates $4–5 Billion Reconstruction Bill
articles.description: Nepal's finance minister estimates that rebuilding after the catastrophic floods could cost between $4 billion and $5 billion. The disaster has destroyed infrastructure, roads, bridges and energy facilities.

articles.title: Niamey Hit by Gunfire and Explosions
articles.description: Sustained gunfire and explosions were reported in several parts of Niamey, including areas near Diori Hamani International Airport and the presidential palace. The cause had not been officially established at the time of reporting, making this a developing story.

articles.title: Iran's Economy Comes Under Severe Pressure
articles.description: Six months into the Iran–US war, Iran is facing severe economic pressure as sanctions intensify, foreign trade declines and oil sales remain disrupted. Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz also remains far below normal levels.

articles.title: Russia–Ukraine Conflict Remains Highly Active
articles.description: Ukraine continues developing its long-range strike capability against Russian targets while Russia maintains attacks against Ukrainian infrastructure. The conflict continues to affect regional security and energy markets.

articles.title: Chinese Chipmaker CXMT Sues Pentagon
articles.description: ChangXin Memory Technologies has filed a lawsuit against the US Department of Defense seeking removal from a Pentagon list identifying it as a Chinese military company. CXMT says its chips are intended for civilian and commercial use.

articles.title: US–China Technology Rivalry Intensifies
articles.description: The CXMT lawsuit adds another chapter to the growing technology dispute between Washington and Beijing, particularly around semiconductors, artificial intelligence and advanced computing.

articles.title: US Military Presence in Europe Remains Under Review
articles.description: The Pentagon is reviewing US military deployments across Europe and preparing several options for future force posture. NATO allies are watching the review closely amid concerns about possible troop reductions.

articles.title: European Energy Markets Watch Strait of Hormuz
articles.description: European governments and energy companies continue monitoring the Strait of Hormuz because disruption to the major energy route could affect fuel prices, gas supplies and inflation.
articles.imageQuery: European energy market oil gas terminal

articles.title: Europe Faces Continued Energy Uncertainty
articles.description: The continuing Iran conflict and disruption around Hormuz are forcing European governments to reassess energy security, supply routes and dependence on vulnerable shipping corridors.

articles.title: Nigeria Receives Positive Moody's Economic Outlook
articles.description: Moody's has changed Nigeria's credit outlook from stable to positive, citing stronger foreign-exchange reserves, economic growth and improved resilience to external shocks. Nigeria's sovereign rating remains B3, with fiscal and debt challenges still identified as risks.

articles.title: Nigeria's Economic Reforms Remain Under Scrutiny
articles.description: Nigeria's improving external position and stronger growth are supporting investor confidence, although fiscal pressure, debt affordability and the cost of living remain important challenges.

articles.title: Nigeria Kidnapping Crisis Remains a Major Security Concern
articles.description: Kidnapping continues to affect communities across Nigeria, with previous research showing the scale of ransom payments and the serious human and economic consequences of the crisis.

articles.title: Dangote Refinery Strengthens Nigeria's Fuel Export Position
articles.description: Nigeria's petroleum-product exports by sea have increased sharply since 2023, with the Dangote refinery contributing significantly to the country's growing role as a regional fuel supplier.

articles.title: Global Markets Watch Iran and Hormuz
articles.description: Investors remain focused on energy prices, inflation, interest rates and geopolitical risks as the Iran conflict continues to disrupt shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: Oil Markets Remain Highly Sensitive to Middle East Developments
articles.description: Oil prices remain closely tied to developments around the Strait of Hormuz. Although some diplomatic efforts have raised hopes of improved shipping, traffic remains well below normal.

articles.title: Global Energy Security Faces Continued Risks
articles.description: The disruption around Hormuz is encouraging countries to examine alternative energy routes, pipelines and ports in an effort to reduce dependence on the strategic waterway.

articles.title: CXMT to Supply LPDDR6 Memory for Xiaomi Foldable Phone
articles.description: Chinese memory-chip manufacturer CXMT says it will supply its latest LPDDR6 DRAM chips for Xiaomi's upcoming 18 Fold smartphone. The development highlights China's growing semiconductor capabilities.

articles.title: China Pushes Forward With Domestic Semiconductor Production
articles.description: CXMT's expansion into LPDDR6 memory production highlights China's efforts to strengthen domestic semiconductor manufacturing and reduce dependence on foreign technology.

articles.title: AI Remains a Major Global Investment Story
articles.description: Artificial intelligence continues to attract enormous investment in computing infrastructure, advanced chips and data centres as investors assess whether the boom can deliver sustainable long-term returns.

morningSummary.title: MORNING SUMMARY
morningSummary.description: The Himalayan disaster is the biggest developing story this morning, with more than 600 deaths and nearly 3,000 people missing across Nepal and Tibet. Bad weather is complicating rescue operations and Nepal estimates reconstruction could cost $4–5 billion. In Niger, gunfire and explosions have been reported across Niamey, but the cause remains unconfirmed. Iran continues to face severe economic pressure as the US intensifies sanctions and shipping through Hormuz remains heavily disrupted. In Nigeria, Moody's has improved the country's credit outlook to positive, while the US–China technology rivalry is intensifying after CXMT sued the Pentagon and announced a major Xiaomi chip deal.

bigQuestion: When breaking news develops faster than authorities can confirm the facts, is it better to share immediately or wait for reliable verification?
